privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.foot: Removes your contact details and exact locations from every report. The de-identified evidence and its signatures stay valid.

card.title: Report {id}

card.gradeNote: The grade is about how strong the evidence is, not about the stream's ecological status. Formal assessment stays with OneAquaHealth's field protocols.
card.whyFoot: Seven readable checks, 100 points. A report without a photo stays at grade C or below.
card.uses: What it may be used for

Citizen stream reports that cities can t: Citizen stream reports that cities can trust
StreamProof grades every citizen stream: StreamProof grades every citizen stream report from A to D with reasons anyone can read, lets neighbours and experts make it stronger, and writes it into OneAquaHealth’s own FHIR standard with a rule for what each trust level may be used for.
A rumour and a verified report look the: A rumour and a verified report look the same to a computer. StreamProof tells them apart inside OneAquaHealth’s own FHIR standard, so cities can act on what citizens see.
Trust in citizen-science data is an old: Trust in citizen-science data is an old problem. Alabri & Hunter (IEEE e-Science 2010) combined quality checks with trust metrics, and Baker et al. (2021) reviewed 259 schemes and recommended layered verification. StreamProof implements that and adds a machine-readable rule for what each trust level may be used for, carried inside standard FHIR records.
It is built for OneAquaHealth’s five cit: It is built for OneAquaHealth’s five cities (Benevento, Coimbra, Ghent, Oslo and Toulouse), works as a module of the HL7 Europe OAH guide, and keeps its rule files open.
Let’s make citizen reports worth acting: Let’s make citizen reports worth acting on
Everything a reviewer asks before trusti: Everything a reviewer asks before trusting a report.
Why not just use iNaturalist’s research: Why not just use iNaturalist’s research grade?
Community agreement isn’t the same as ac: Community agreement isn’t the same as accuracy for hard-to-identify taxa, and a research-grade label doesn’t say what a record may be used for. StreamProof adds both: reasons for the grade and a rule for each use.
They scored trust. StreamProof turns tru: They scored trust. StreamProof turns trust into enforceable use rules and carries them inside a health-data standard, following the layered verification Baker et al. (2021) recommend.
OneAquaHealth’s own data guide, maintain: OneAquaHealth’s own data guide, maintained by HL7 Europe, is FHIR, and its health partners already speak it. In One Digital Health, stream data and health data travel in the same format.
They are configurable defaults, meant to: They are configurable defaults, meant to be calibrated with OAH ecologists. A calibration report publishes the current limits and the numbers behind them.
Can a group fake a signal?: Can a group fake a signal?
It takes different people, spread in tim: It takes different people, spread in time or place, under a daily cap and weighted by track record, plus an expert for decision grade. The threshold counts people, not reports.
Reporters are pseudonymous, FHIR records: Reporters are pseudonymous, FHIR records carry a location coarsened to about 100 m, identities sit in a separate vault, and erasure keeps the signed evidence valid. A real deployment still needs review by a data protection officer.
Is it connected to the OAH app and Dipte: Is it connected to the OAH app and DipteraCAST?
StreamProof is designed to sit behind On: StreamProof is designed to sit behind OneAquaHealth’s Citizen Science App as a trust layer. For DipteraCAST it exports verified ground truth; the model itself isn’t public.
Why not put it on a blockchain?: Why not put it on a blockchain?
An Ed25519 signature over a de-identifie: An Ed25519 signature over a de-identified hash is tamper-evident and simple, and it still lets a person’s identity be erased. A blockchain would add cost without adding trust here.

Report, grade, strengthen, release. Rule: Report, grade, strengthen, release. Rules and the community check most reports and experts check the flagged ones, so reviewers spend their time only where it matters.
A citizen or a school group takes a phot: A citizen or a school group takes a photo and taps the signs they can see: scum, foam, a bad smell, dead fish, mosquitoes, stagnant water, an oily sheen, sewage or litter, or “everything looks fine”. The public location is coarsened to about 100 m and the reporter stays pseudonymous.
Seven readable checks (photo, time, GPS,: Seven readable checks (photo, time, GPS, on-stream position, nearby reports, weather and track record) give a grade from A to D, each with a reason in plain words. The grade measures evidence quality, never ecological status: formal assessment stays with OAH field protocols.
Independent neighbours corroborate, coun: Independent neighbours corroborate, counted as people rather than reports, under a daily cap. An expert can verify directly at a rural site. Missions send volunteers to reaches with few reports, so evidence doesn’t only follow well-walked areas.
A permitted-use gate reads a published F: A permitted-use gate reads a published FHIR rule file before anything leaves. Expert-verified records are written in the OAH guide’s format, and decision-grade evidence can raise an advisory that a site “may warrant inspection”, never a diagnosis.
OneAquaHealth’s FHIR guide records what: OneAquaHealth’s FHIR guide records what was observed, but not how far it can be trusted or what it may be used for. Here’s what StreamProof adds.
A to D from seven checks a citizen can r: A to D from seven checks a citizen can read, mapped to the ISO 19157 data-quality elements: positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic accuracy, completeness and logical consistency.
What each trust level may be used for (o: What each trust level may be used for (org dashboard, public map, OAH export, certificate, advisory, DipteraCAST) is published as a FHIR CodeSystem that the gate loads at startup.
Profiles derive from ObservationIndicato: Profiles derive from ObservationIndicatorsOah and LocationOah: the OAH indicator goes in the code, the citizen’s sign in the value. Six of nine signs map to OAH concepts; the other three are proposed as new ones.
A River Health Brief with measures match: A River Health Brief with measures matched from the OAH Catalogue of Measures, expert-verified Diptera presence and absence for DipteraCAST, and a signed certificate for every contributor.
